To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new approach to measure the absolute characteristics of the electron beams emitted by a medical accelerator, and that this approach is based on the measurement of the electron beam with a calibrated image plate placed in the magnetic spectrometer, which is used to infer the absolute energy spectrum from the measured data.
the energy spectrum of the electron beam can be measured using a magnetic spectrometers and image plates.
the energy distribution of the electrons emitted from a medical linear accelerator can be measured by means of a magnetic spectrometry system and a calibrated image plate detector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the absolute characterization of an electron beam using a spectrometer.
the development of an experimental method to measure the absolute electron energy spectrum of an electron beam emitted from a medical accelerator and to compare it with Monte Carlo simulations.
the absolute characterization of a clinical accelerator and its application for the evaluation of the accuracy of Monte Carlo codes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is an important first step in the development of a methodology for the absolute characterization of a clinical electron beam using a spectrometer and Monte Carlo simulations.
the absolute energy distribution obtained with the present experimental method is in very good agreement with the Monte Carlo simulation.

the absolute energy distribution measured in the present study is consistent with that obtained from the Monte Carlo simulations and that the contribution of direct electrons is negligible in the depth dose curve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy distribution of a Varian 2100C medical electron beam is measured and the results are compared to the ones obtained by Monte Carlo simulations.
we were able to characterize the electron beam delivered from the medical accelerator using an original experimental setup and a Monte Carlo code.

we have developed a new method for measuring the absolute energy distribution and energy spectra of electrons emitted from a medical accelerator, which is a very difficult task, and we have demonstrated that the method can be used to measure the electron beam energy distribution and spectra emitted from a medical electron linear accelerator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the direct electrons contribute to the dose at the depth of the maximum dose, and that the contribution is significant at the level of the 5 % of the maximum dose.
the direct electrons emitted by the Varian 21EX electron accelerator are not negligible and should be considered in the treatment planning.
the magnetic spectrometer is able to characterize an electron beam at the isocentry of a clinical accelerator, with an accuracy of about 1%.
